item: six skill filenames from Brownian-Dynamics-Agent, and the same vocabulary echoed under three other local project paths. DELIBERATELY NOT TRANSCRIBED HERE: writing them into this repository's disk would be the import the rule exists to prevent, so this row records the count and the channel and not the strings. A later auditor who needs them can read the same source; a later designer who does not need them should not meet them in a ledger.
rule: CLAUDE.md, 'The prior repositories -- three closed, one open under rules'. Brownian-Dynamics-Agent is one of the three CLOSED, so 10.2.1's three-way ruling does not really apply: there is no open row, so no slot can be named, and 10.2.1 says an item unable to name a place is discarded. The rule that makes filenames count at all is the same paragraph: 'This covers filenames, not just contents: a filename carries vocabulary, and vocabulary carries design.'
by: architecture, standing. This seat exercised no judgement -- the prohibition is flat for a closed repository, and recording it as a ruling would overstate what happened if `by` were this seat. 7.1 rule 9 says `by` names the judgement and not the hand, and here the hand and the judgement are different layers.
how_it_arrived: unbidden, and that is the part worth keeping. This seat did not consult the repository. The person pasted ~/.claude.json into the session to ask an unrelated question -- where to add an MCP approval -- and that file's per-project records carry `loggedAuthoredArtifactPaths` and `skillUsage` for every project on this machine, the closed repositories included.
why_this_is_a_second_channel: CLAUDE.md records the first one and says it is closed: until 2026-09-16 a SessionStart hook injected ~/.claude/knowledge/ into every session, and 'its filenames did leak terminology into this design'. The hook is gone. The machine's own configuration is a second path to the same vocabulary, it was never named, and nothing in this repository can close it -- the file is outside the repository and is read by the harness, not by us. Raised with architecture; 10.2 and 10.3 are plan.md's.
what_a_drop_can_and_cannot_mean_here: it cannot mean deletion. The names are in this session's context and cannot be removed from it, so the ruling is a commitment rather than an erasure: they influence nothing this seat writes, and naming them here is what makes that checkable instead of merely asserted. CLAUDE.md's own account of the first leak is the reason to distrust a silent 'I did not use it' -- that leak happened to sessions that were not trying to import anything either.
no_check_reads_this_file: ALLOWED_PATHS permits the path and nothing validates the shape, so these fields were matched by hand against the spec in plan.md section 7 rather than against microscope_agent/rulings.jsonl -- reading another agent's ledger for a format that design already declares is the 6.2 rule 3 crossing this seat self-reported earlier today in 1a69237. The spec was reachable inside the boundary, so the crossing was avoidable.
